claims: Almost all male U.S. citizens and male immigrants living in the U.S. aged 18–25 must register with the Selective Service System.
Selective Service System registration is a legal requirement.
Automatic Selective Service System registration is launching in 2026 for many.
Male citizens and immigrants including undocumented, refugees, and asylum seekers born in 1960 or later living in the U.S. between 18 and 25 years old must register with the Selective Service System.
Selective Service System registration must occur within 30 days of turning 18.
Late Selective Service System registration is accepted until age 26.
Selective Service System registration can be completed online at SSS.gov.
Selective Service System registration can be completed at a U.S. Post Office.
Selective Service System registration can be completed via registration forms.
Starting in 2026, many states automatically register eligible men through driver’s license or ID applications.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to felony charges.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to $250,000 in fines.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for federal and state-based student grants and loans.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for federal job training and employment.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to ineligibility for U.S. citizenship for immigrants.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to fines up to $250,000.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System can lead to up to five years in prison.
Selective Service System registration is not a sign-up for the military.
Selective Service System registration is a list to be used if Congress and the President authorize a draft.
Registrants must notify the Selective Service of address changes until age 26.
Women are currently not required to register with the Selective Service System.
